title: Serum Institute to Manufacture World's First New TB Vaccine in a Century
excerpt: India's largest vaccine maker partners with Gates Medical Research Institute to produce M72/AS01E, investing over $100 million to prepare for potential approval of a shot that could prevent 76 million new TB cases globally.
body:
• Serum Institute of India has signed an agreement with the Gates Medical Research Institute to manufacture M72/AS01E, a tuberculosis vaccine candidate that could become the first new TB vaccine in over 100 years.
  • Serum Institute plans to invest more than $100 million to scale up manufacturing capacity ahead of potential regulatory approval.
  • The vaccine showed approximately 50 percent efficacy against active pulmonary TB in Phase 2b trials. A Phase 3 trial with 20,000 participants is fully enrolled across five countries.
  • India carries the world's highest tuberculosis burden. The WHO estimates a vaccine with this efficacy could prevent 76 million new TB cases and save 8.5 million lives over 25 years.

A Century-Old Gap in TB Prevention

Serum Institute of India, the world's largest vaccine manufacturer by volume, announced Thursday that it will manufacture an experimental tuberculosis vaccine under an agreement with the Gates Medical Research Institute — a deal that could reshape the global fight against humanity's deadliest infectious disease.

The vaccine candidate, M72/AS01E, has been in development for two decades. If approved, it would be the first new TB vaccine since the Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) shot was introduced in 1921. While BCG is effective at preventing severe TB in young children, it offers poor protection against pulmonary TB in adults and adolescents — the group that accounts for 89 percent of new TB cases worldwide.

How the Partnership Works

Under the agreement, Gates MRI — founded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation — will transfer the technology and know-how needed to manufacture the M72 vaccine antigen, enabling Serum Institute to prepare for large-scale production, according to Reuters. GlaxoSmithKline, which originally developed the vaccine candidate, will supply the AS01E adjuvant that boosts the body's immune response.

Serum Institute plans to invest more than $100 million to build out manufacturing capacity and prepare for future supply, pending approval. The company was selected based on its track record of producing WHO-prequalified vaccines affordably and at scale, the partners said in a joint statement.

"Initiating this work well ahead of Phase III trial results is a deliberate strategy to ensure readiness to produce and distribute the vaccine and begin meeting global demand as quickly as possible, should the trial be successful and regulatory approvals be granted."

— Gates MRI and Serum Institute joint statement

What the Trials Show

Gates MRI is sponsoring the Phase 3 clinical trial of M72/AS01E, funded by the Gates Foundation and Wellcome, a major London-based health charity. The double-blind, randomized trial started in March 2024 and reached full enrollment in April 2025, with 20,000 participants across 54 sites in South Africa, Kenya, Malawi, Zambia, and Indonesia, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

In an earlier Phase 2b trial with 3,575 participants, the vaccine demonstrated approximately 50 percent protection against progression to active pulmonary TB over a three-year follow-up period in TB-infected, HIV-negative adults aged 18 to 50. The WHO estimates that a vaccine with this efficacy profile could prevent 76 million new TB cases, save 8.5 million lives, and save $41.5 billion for TB-affected households over 25 years.

India's TB Crisis

The stakes are particularly high for India. The country carries the world's highest tuberculosis burden, with an estimated 2.8 million new cases annually. Tuberculosis remains a leading cause of death in India, disproportionately affecting low-income communities. Nearly 11 million people contracted TB globally in 2024, while 1.23 million died from the disease, according to WHO data.

For the Indian diaspora, Serum Institute's role in manufacturing the vaccine underscores the company's growing centrality to global public health. Serum Institute already produces more than 1.5 billion vaccine doses annually, including a significant share of the world's childhood immunizations. The company played a critical role in COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing through its production of the Oxford-AstraZeneca shot as Covishield.

What Comes Next

The Phase 3 trial results are expected to take several years, given the trial's size and scope. The partners have also committed to engaging local manufacturers in Indonesia and South Africa to support critical parts of the supply chain over time. If regulatory approvals are granted, the partnership aims to make the vaccine available to adults and adolescents in countries with the highest TB burden as quickly as possible.
